subject: Is there trick to forcing legend when 'y' is mapped in geom (instead of ggplot)?

messages.author: 92a46c9449c605e2
messages.subject: Is there trick to forcing legend when 'y' is mapped in geom (instead of ggplot)?
parts:
I'm using "legend=TRUE" in geoms on chart, yet no legend is
displayed. Is that because 'y' is mapped in the geom functions
instead of in the ggplot function?

df <- data.frame(index=1:5, A=runif(5), B=runif(5))
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x=index))
p <- p + geom_point(aes(y=A), color="blue", legend=TRUE) +
geom_line(aes(y=A), color="blue", legend=TRUE)
p <- p + geom_point(aes(y=B), color="green", legend=TRUE) +
geom_line(aes(y=B), color="green", legend=TRUE)
p


Any help would be appreciated,
Mauricio

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: Is there trick to forcing legend when 'y' is mapped in geom (instead of ggplot)?
parts: Hi Mauricio,

On Tue, Aug 2, 2011 at 12:01 PM, Mauricio <Maurici...@yahoo.com> wrote:
> I'm using "legend=TRUE" in geoms on chart, yet no legend is
> displayed.  Is that because 'y' is mapped in the geom functions
> instead of in the ggplot function?

No, it's because no aesthetic is mapped. To get the automatically
generated legend, you need to map a variable to an aesthetic.

>
> df <- data.frame(index=1:5, A=runif(5), B=runif(5))
> p <- ggplot(df, aes(x=index))
> p <- p + geom_point(aes(y=A), color="blue", legend=TRUE) +
> geom_line(aes(y=A), color="blue", legend=TRUE)
> p <- p + geom_point(aes(y=B), color="green", legend=TRUE) +
> geom_line(aes(y=B), color="green", legend=TRUE)
> p

Try this:

dat <- melt(df, id = "index")
ggplot(dat, aes(x = index, y = value, color = variable)) +
geom_point() + geom_line()

Best,
Ista

>
>
> Any help would be appreciated,
> Mauricio

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Is there trick to forcing legend when 'y' is mapped in geom (instead of ggplot)?
parts:
Hi:

You could also do this:

df <- data.frame(index=1:5, A=runif(5), B=runif(5))
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x=index))

p <- p + geom_point(aes(y=A, color="blue")) +
geom_line(aes(y=A, color="blue"))
p <- p + geom_point(aes(y=B, color="green")) +
geom_line(aes(y=B, color="green"))
p # oops...

# Add the following to get the right colors
p + scale_color_manual('color', values= c('blue' = 'blue', 'green' = 'green'))

This indicates that mapping the colors one by one generates a factor
variable with the given colors as factor levels. As a result, you need
the manual scale to map the correct colors to the factor levels.

Ista's method is preferred and the way I would suggest to go. This is
an example where reshaping the data simplifies the ggplot() code
immensely, making it much easier to read and understand.

Dennis

While that worked, the chart produced two legends: one for the color
and one for the linetype. Might you know if there's an approach to

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Is there trick to forcing legend when 'y' is mapped in geom (instead of ggplot)?
parts:
The usual way to merge two legends is to make sure they have the same
title, the same breaks and the same values (and if you change the
labels, they need to be the same, too).

Here's an 'easy' reproducible example: map the same factor to two aesthetics.

d <- data.frame(gp = factor(rep(LETTERS[1:4], each = 10)),
x = rep(1:10, 4),
y = rep(1:4, each = 10) +
rep(c(0.5, 0.7, 1, 1.2), each = 10) * rep(1:10, 4) +
rnorm(40))
ggplot(d, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = gp, linetype = gp)) +
geom_point(size = 2.5) + geom_line(size = 1) +
labs(colour = 'Group', linetype = 'Group', y = 'Response')

Since the default title is the factor name 'gp', to change the title
to 'Group' in the merged legend I need to change the name of each
legend title. If you change one but not the other, you get two
legends; if the legends are given different names, you'll get two
legends.

HTH,
Dennis
